newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa police claim some success in war on crime.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa police claim some success in war on crime.

text.p: South African police on Monday claimed some success in their war on crime, saying that all violent crime figures except rape showed a downward trend.

The murder rate in the eight months to August fell by 9.6 percent compared to the same period last year, with an average 37 people out of every 100,000 being killed, policing minister Sydney Mufamadi told a news conference.
Other crimes showing a downward trend in South Africa, one of the world's most violent societies, were armed robbery, attempted murder and drug-related crimes.
Despite the successes the fight against criminals would continue, he added. "We have not won the war on crime. We must not become triumphalist."
Among reasons cited for falling crime figures were use of special investigative teams, improved crime intelligence and better cooperation from communities.
But rape had jumped by 4.5 percent in the first eight months of 1996 compared to a year earlier, according to crime statistician Chris de Kock.
"We have the highest rape figures in the world," he said, adding that the higher figure could be attributed to increased reporting of sex crimes.

South Africa's business capital Gauteng still suffered most from vehicle hijackings and housebreaking. But the sparsely populated semi-desert Northern Cape province was where people were "most likely to be murdered, raped or assaulted" due to high incidences of domestic violence, alcohol and drug abuse.
